source.label: Two user-supplied tactical game UI references

context.surface: main menu, loadout and pause menu

observations.evidence: The first reference uses an oversized title, one large operator silhouette and a compact diagonal action stack.
observations.interpretation: Keep one dominant operative and one obvious action rail instead of distributing attention evenly.

observations.evidence: Both references are mostly charcoal and black, with rare saturated status accents.
observations.interpretation: Use cyan for system identity and yellow only for action, readiness and separators.

observations.evidence: The second reference groups equipment in rigid framed modules and consistent cells.
observations.interpretation: Treat loadout and pause information as separate technical cards with strong alignment.

observations.evidence: Dark metal frames, fine lines and worn overlays create a utilitarian field rather than a glossy consumer UI.
observations.interpretation: Prefer square panels, thin borders and low-contrast technical lines over rounded glass cards.

rules.rule: Use a split hero field with the operative on the left and the action rail on the right.
rules.evidence: The first reference separates a dominant character mass from its navigation stack.

rules.rule: Group loadout, status and controls into bordered modules sharing a common alignment system.
rules.evidence: The inventory reference is legible because each information family owns one bounded panel.

rules.rule: Reserve yellow for primary interaction and cyan for identity or live-system state.
rules.evidence: Rare color accents direct attention against an almost monochrome field.

rules.rule: Keep decorative graphics behind information and below text contrast thresholds.
rules.evidence: Reference textures establish mood without replacing the main navigation hierarchy.

anti_rules: Do not copy a reference logo, title treatment, operator identity or exact wording.
Do not reproduce the inventory item artwork or the exact three-window arrangement.
Do not cover every surface in bright accent color.
Do not use rounded mobile-style cards for the tactical shell.

protected_elements: reference game logo and typography lockup
exact menu wording and screen composition
